source.title: Polymorphism Is Rotation: Operational Mechanistic Interpretability from a Two-Layer Transformer to Pythia-70m

record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests SAE feature transfer and reconstruction across independently trained models. It argues that decoder-cosine universality is incomplete evidence of functional feature universality, and reports failures without alignment and recovery after an orthogonal rotation.
record.gate_note: Relevant results concern SAE decoder matching, cross-seed SAE reconstruction, and SAE firing-pattern transfer. The rotation, steering, mechanistic-bar, and attribution-patching results do not directly test the listed superposition or polysemanticity claims. The paper does not measure feature sparsity, competition for capacity, importance-dependent feature geometry, or feature dimensionality.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-seed and cross-checkpoint SAE feature stability: decoder matching, reconstruction and firing-pattern agreement, raw and after Procrustes rotation. These results bear on V5's stability and canonicality. It argues decoder cosine alone does not establish functional feature universality. It does not test sparse-feature recovery as evidence of superposition in LLMs (V4), capacity, polysemanticity origins or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors further conclude that SAE dictionaries are universal up to rotation: features universalise as rotation-equivalence classes, and cross-seed bases are Haar-random rotations. They note a residual non-orthogonal component in firing patterns near the unembed. Frontier-scale replication is left open.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures SAE transfer and residual-stream Procrustes alignment rather than testing feature superposition or a sparsity-dependent geometry. The supplied text does not specify the original method in enough detail for a closer recipe comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by site: Pythia decoder matching falls at the final residual site, post-rotation reconstruction is lower at layer0 resid pre, and firing-pattern recovery is weakest near the unembed-bound output. Checkpoint transfer also differs between the reported toy and Pythia comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-seed residual-stream bases differ by a Haar-uniform random rotation; ‖R−I‖F matches √(2d) and the KS test against Haar gives p≈1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained transformers share representations up to an arbitrary orthogonal basis rotation.

fits_no_version.finding: Toy MLPs use all 256 neurons with 67k–145k activation patterns, described as distributed quantisation rather than single-neuron features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distributed MLP coding in a small algorithmic transformer; not an LLM and not tied to capacity.

record.code_released: Supplementary code archive is stated; URL not stated.
record.problems: The paper tests only a 104,448-parameter Dyck-3 toy and Pythia-70m, not frontier-scale models. Some SAE outcomes are reported as ranges aggregated across sites or pairs. The Pythia checkpoint comparison is a single model, checkpoint pair, and layer. Post-rotation firing correlations remain below the within-seed reference.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant SAE reconstruction, decoder-cosine, or firing-pattern result was omitted. Other reported outcomes, including steering transfer, weight alignment, behavioral KL, patching, and ablation measurements, do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: No toy superposition with sparse features, sparsity-dependent transition or geometry.
No analysis of the origins of polysemantic neurons.
No measure of feature sparsity or SAE interpretability in Pythia; cross-seed reconstruction does not test whether sparse features exist.
Completeness, and canonicality across SAE size or hyperparameters, are not tested; only cross-seed and cross-checkpoint stability is.

missing.what: Pythia mean max-cosine of matched decoder columns, 0.91–0.93
Within-seed SAE self-EV values and SAE sparsity (L0) are not reported numerically, apart from the Pythia layer-3 self-EV of 0.907

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label for V5 rested on raw unaligned transfer. The authors attribute that failure to basis rotation, not to different features, so those rows are recoded as cannot_determine. Internal tension: decoder columns reportedly match across seeds without rotation, yet bases are claimed to be Haar-random rotations. This is unexplained in the text and worth caution. Single-author preprint; small models only.

versions.untested_parts: No test of sparse-feature superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular feature geometry in small networks.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemanticity caused by limited capacity.
No test of whether polysemantic neurons arise through mechanisms other than capacity pressure.

Tests SAE reconstruction and firing-pattern transfer, including after rotation, but does not establish that real-model features are sparse in the claim's sense, spread across many neurons, or exhaustively recovered.
Tests decoder-column matching and functional SAE transfer across seeds and checkpoints; does not establish completeness or canonicality across architectures, tasks, or other alignment procedures.
No comparison of one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: Decoder-column matching and post-rotation reconstruction at intermediate and internal sites, toy and Pythia-70m
relationships.reason: ≥98–99% of decoder columns match across seeds (R8, R10). Post-rotation reconstruction is 0.97–0.99 on the toy and up to 0.99 on Pythia, and 0.98–0.999 across toy checkpoints (R4, R7, R12, R20).
relationships.display_finding: At least 98–99% of decoder columns matched across seeds, and post-rotation reconstruction was 0.97–0.99 on the toy, up to 0.99 on Pythia, and 0.98–0.999 across toy checkpoints.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Decoder-column matching and post-rotation reconstruction at intermediate and internal sites, toy and Pythia-70m
source_check.reason: R8 and R10 show nearly complete decoder matching; R4, R12 and R20 show high reconstruction after alignment, with R7 reporting Pythia recovery up to 0.99. These support stability under the specified metrics and alignment.

relationships.condition: Feature-level firing agreement after rotation; final residual layer; Pythia cross-checkpoint transfer
relationships.reason: Post-rotation firing correlation is only 0.25–0.44 on Pythia and 0.27–0.74 on the toy, with 15–51% of features above r 0.5 (R14, R17, R18). Final-layer decoder match is 62% (R9). Pythia checkpoint EV is 0.73 vs self 0.907 (R22).
relationships.display_finding: Post-rotation firing correlation was only 0.25–0.44 on Pythia and 0.27–0.74 on the toy model, with 15–51% of features above r = 0.5. Final-layer decoder match was 62%, and cross-checkpoint explained variance on Pythia was 0.73 vs 0.907 for the model itself.

relation.reason: The study directly measures cross-model and cross-checkpoint dictionary agreement, reconstruction transfer, and feature firing agreement.

tranche.reason: Decoder agreement coexists with poor direct transfer and incomplete firing recovery; the results qualify V5's stability and canonicality and motivate equivalence up to rotation.

source_check.notes: The authors conclude universality up to rotation while reporting incomplete firing recovery. These cross-base-model and checkpoint comparisons do not establish dictionary-wide equivalence across independent SAE seeds on one fixed LLM; frontier-scale replication remains untested.

statements.correction: Pythia-70m: nine independently trained seeds; intermediate-layer decoder matching ≥99% above cosine 0.5. Dyck-3 Cohort A: post-rotation EV 0.976–0.990; seeds 1–4 use seed0's trained input/output weights, frozen during training.
statements.problem: The numerical claims match, but the independent-base-model condition needs qualification for the toy result: Cohort A shares frozen input/output weights.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE transfer after Procrustes alignment, in the tested toy and Pythia settings
reader_labels.reason: Aligned SAE reconstruction is high: 0.976–0.990 on the toy and 0.85–0.99 on Pythia, with independent-init toy results of 0.965–0.987 (R4, R7, R12).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Unaligned cross-seed SAE transfer on the toy and Pythia models
reader_labels.reason: The SAE encoder does not transfer functionally despite high decoder-column cosine: raw reconstruction is negative at every internal toy site and negative at later Pythia sites, while decoder matches remain high at many sites (R1, R6, R8, R10).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: After orthogonal alignment and at particular layers or checkpoints
reader_labels.reason: Rotation restores much, but not uniformly all, reconstruction or firing-pattern agreement; Pythia reconstruction spans 0.85–0.99, firing correlations remain below self-correlation, and final-layer decoder matching falls to 62% (R7, R9, R14, R17, R18, R20, R22).
